title: Point Transformer V3: Simpler, Faster, Stronger
layout_note: A 2x2 grid of serialization patterns - Z-order and Hilbert on top, their transposed variants below - each a row of three square grids: the curve alone, the curve threading a toy point set, the point path that remains.
grouping: No frames: each pattern is a triplet of equal square grids under a bold serif label '(a) Z-order' ... '(d) Trans Hilbert'; the four triplets sit in a 2x2 arrangement with transposed variants directly below their base pattern.
shapes_depth: Flat, monochrome line art: light-grey square grids, a dark-grey space-filling polyline with an arrowhead, small hollow grey circles for points over light-grey letter-shaped blobs, and dark-grey polylines joining points; one segment in (c) is dark blue.
proposed_highlight: No highlight: the whole figure is the paper's serialization step; the four patterns are told apart only by panel labels and the curve's shape.
lesson: Show an ordering operation on one small toy point set reused in every panel - curve alone, curve over the points, the path left behind - so only the pattern changes between panels.
notes: Venue written as arXiv: the arXiv v2 PDF's first pages state no venue; the candidate list gives CVPR 2024 (unverified). year = arXiv preprint year. 'other' element: space-filling-curve polylines over a toy point set. Method name PTv3 from the caption. The architecture figure (Fig. 6) is a plain monochrome box row with asterisks for new parts and was not carded; Fig. 4 (patch grouping) has a dense tangle of reorder arrows.

arrangement.units: four unframed triplets of square grids in a 2x2 arrangement, each under a bold '(a)'-style label
arrangement.inputs_as: the same toy point set sits in the middle and right grid of every triplet: small hollow circles over light-grey letter-shaped blobs standing for a point cloud
arrangement.shared: the same toy point set is reused in all four patterns

taxonomy.task: point-cloud serialization by space-filling curves for patch attention in a point transformer

core.what: each space-filling curve is drawn on a small toy point set: the curve alone on a grid, the curve threading the points, then the dark point-to-point path it leaves - the serialization shown as geometry on the data

relations.form: points as hollow circles on a grid over a letter-shaped blob, joined by a polyline in the order the curve visits them
four identical triplets in a 2x2 grid, base patterns on top and their transposed variants directly below
within each triplet three equal grids left to right: curve, curve plus points, resulting path - no arrows between them

channels.colour: grey value only: dark grey = the active curve or path, light grey = grid, faded curve and the blob under the points; one dark-blue segment in (c) has no key
channels.shape: hollow circle = point, square cell = space partition, polyline = visiting order
channels.line: solid polyline with arrowheads = traversal order; thin light lines = grid
channels.frame: none; panel labels group the triplets

quality.strengths: The method's step is drawn on a small instance of the structure; the same toy point set is reused in every panel so only the curve changes; each triplet decomposes the step into curve -> overlay -> path; transposed variants sit directly under their base pattern so the transposition reads by vertical comparison.
quality.weaknesses: Curve and path are separated only by grey value, and in the middle grid the faded curve, grid, blob and arrowed path overlap so the order is hard to trace; nothing marks the three grids as steps; the single blue segment in (c) is unexplained; the figure stops at the ordering and does not show the patches it feeds.

insights.structure: A 2x2 grid of pattern triplets, base patterns above their transposed variants, each triplet three equal square grids in a row.
insights.data: The point cloud is a toy set of hollow circles over light-grey letter-shaped blobs, reused unchanged in all four patterns.
insights.emphasis: None: monochrome throughout, the patterns told apart by bold serif labels and the curve's shape.
insights.flow: Left to right inside a triplet (curve, overlay, path) with no connecting arrows; comparison runs across the 2x2 grid.
insights.avoid: Do not overlay a faded curve, a grid and an arrowed path in the same grey family - give the resulting order its own colour.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
